newsitem.title: GREECE: Strikes sweep Greece in protest at budget.
newsitem.headline: Strikes sweep Greece in protest at budget.

text.p: Greek workers crippled transport, schools, hospitals and public services with a 24-hour strike Thursday to protest against the ruling socialists' new austerity budget.

Government and union officials said the strike disrupted air, sea, train and urban transport. No buses or trolleys and only a few taxis appeared in Athens, while government ministries operated with reduced staffs.
Many public sector workers, including those at state banks, followed the strike, but it was largely ignored by private sector workers, officials said.
Farmers, demanding higher price supports and fuel susidies, blocked the main north-south national road with 2,000 tractors, halting traffic between the capital and Greece's second city of Salonika.
The strike was called to protest against the 1997 austerity budget, due to be presented on Friday.
National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou has said the budget will be the toughest in 15 years as Greece struggles to get its economy in line with its European Union partners.

Papandoniou and Prime Minister Costas Simitis have said that their priority is joining Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) by 2001, two years after the first wave of EU states are due to create a single common currency.
Papandoniou has vowed to tax only the wealthy but he has rejected numerous requests from organised labour to ease the economic hardship of lower paid workers.
"This government feels for the problems of the workers, and especially the weaker social strata and asks for understanding," a government statement said Thursday.
But it said its austerity plan and a strong drachma policy to fight inflation were the best ways to support the real income of wage earners, pensioners and farmers.
"The new taxes in the 1997 budget will fall exclusively on higher incomes," it said.
The General Confederation of Greek Workers (GSEE), the main public and private sector group with some three million members, called the stike. The union of civil servants (ADEDY) joined in.
"GSEE expresses its full rejection of the announced economic austerity policy and will fight for protection and improvement of the income of workers and pensioners," a statement said.

Workers at state-run Olympic Airways staged a three-hour stoppage in the morning, delaying international and domestic flights. Civil aviation employees, except traffic controllers, have called for a three-hour stoppage in the evening.
Some 8,000 to 10,000 GSEE and ADEDY workers marched through Athens to the national economy ministry to demand the budget be amended before being voted on in parliament next month.
The budget includes the abolition of most tax exemptions and cuts state spending to meet the Maastricht Treaty economic criteria required for joining EMU.
Greece is the only EU country that has failed to meet any of the criteria for joining EMU.
